subject: Cognitive Science
title: Synesthesia
description: A fast breakdown of Synesthesia for builders.

hook.text: For some people, the number 5 is always red, Tuesday tastes like chicken, and music paints colors in the air.

buildup.text: Synesthesia is involuntary cross-wiring of senses. About 4% of the population experiences some form of it.

discovery.text: Brain imaging shows that synesthetes have extra connections between sensory regions that most people lack.

twist.text: Babies may all be synesthetic. The mass pruning of neural connections in infancy might separate the senses in most people.

climax.text: Synesthesia is consistent for life—if 5 is red at age 7, it's red at age 70. It's a structural brain trait, not imagination.

punchline.text: Some brains never fully separated the senses.
